cards.title: Three hearts
cards.text: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood through the gills and one pumps it around the body. Its blood is blue because it uses copper-based haemocyanin to carry oxygen.

cards.title: Nearly indestructible
cards.text: Tardigrades, or water bears, can survive drying out for years, extreme cold and even exposure to the vacuum of space by entering a dormant state.

cards.title: Fast grower
cards.text: Some bamboo species can grow close to a metre in a single day, making them among the fastest-growing plants on Earth.

cards.title: Biggest ever
cards.text: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived, reaching around 30 metres long. Its heart alone is about the size of a small car.

cards.title: Ocean breath
cards.text: Roughly half of the oxygen produced on Earth comes from the ocean, mostly from tiny photosynthesising plankton.

cards.question: What is the fastest land animal?
cards.explanation: Cheetahs can sprint at around 100–110 km/h in short bursts.

cards.question: Which of these mammals lays eggs?
cards.explanation: Platypuses and echidnas, the monotremes, are the only egg-laying mammals.

cards.question: How do honeybees tell each other where flowers are?
What is the largest desert on Earth?
cards.explanation: A desert is defined by low precipitation, not heat. Antarctica is the largest; the Sahara is the largest hot desert.

cards.question: How many legs does a spider have?

cards.statement: Goldfish have a memory span of only three seconds.
cards.explanation: Experiments show goldfish can remember things for months and can be trained to respond to sounds and colours.
All bats can see. Many also use echolocation, and some fruit bats have excellent vision.

cards.statement: Ostriches bury their heads in the sand when scared.
cards.explanation: They lower their heads to turn their eggs in ground nests or lie flat to hide, which may look like burying from afar.

cards.statement: Sharks have existed for longer than trees.
cards.explanation: Sharks appear in the fossil record around 400+ million years ago; the first trees appeared around 385 million years ago.

cards.statement: Chameleons change colour mainly to blend in with their surroundings.
cards.explanation: Colour change is mostly about communication, mood and temperature control rather than camouflage.

cards.statement: Koalas can sleep up to 20 hours a day.
cards.explanation: Their eucalyptus diet is low in energy, so they rest most of the day.
Bowhead whales are among the longest-lived mammals.
In a hunting stoop, the peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth.
